::: proof
We sketch the argument for a scalar parameter
and the point null hypothesis $H_0: \param = \param_0$,
which imposes $q = 1$ constraint.
For the full proof, see [@wilks1938] or [@dobson4e, Section 5.7].

By @exr-wilks-lrt-quadratic,
$\lrstat \approx \oinf(\hthml)(\hthml - \param_0)^2$.
Under the regularity conditions,
$\oinf(\hthml)/\einf(\param_0) \to 1$ in probability,
by the law of large numbers and the consistency of $\hthml$;
this sketch assumes that step rather than proving it.
So, with $Z$ as in @exr-wilks-std-gaussian:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lrstat
&\approx \oinf(\hthml)(\hthml - \param_0)^2
&& \text{(quadratic approximation to $\lrstat$)}\\
&\approx \einf(\param_0)(\hthml - \param_0)^2
&& \text{($\oinf(\hthml)/\einf(\param_0) \to 1$)}\\
&= \paren{\sqrt{\einf(\param_0)}\,(\hthml - \param_0)}^2
&& \text{(write the product as a square)}\\
&= Z^2
&& \text{(definition of $Z$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

By @thm-dist-mle, $\hthml \dsim \ndist{\param_0, \einf(\param_0)^{-1}}$ under $H_0$,
so by @exr-wilks-std-gaussian,
$\lrstat \approx Z^2$ has approximately a $\chi^2_1$ distribution.

With $q$ constraints, the same argument in matrix form
makes $\lrstat$ approximately a sum of $q$ squared,
independent standard Gaussian variables,
which has a $\chi^2_q$ distribution;
this sketch does not derive the matrix form.
:::
